issues.legal_issue: The right to seek a reference to arbitration accrues, for limitation purposes, when genuine efforts to resolve the dispute amicably have ended and resort to adjudication becomes necessary.
material_facts: The parties’ dissolution arrangement provided for arbitration of disputes concerning the partnership and its winding up.
After disagreement arose over distribution of the dissolved firm’s properties, the parties appointed nominees and exchanged correspondence while trying to reach an amicable arrangement.
The correspondence showed continuing efforts to implement the arrangement; the Court found that the application was filed within the limitation period when measured from the final communication.
issues.conclusion: The application was within time. The right to apply accrued only after the parties’ efforts to resolve the matter amicably had run their course, rather than when the properties were not distributed or nominees were appointed.
issues.legal_principle: Article 137 of the Limitation Act, 1963 applies to an application under Section 20 of the Arbitration Act, 1940, and time runs from when the right to apply accrues. Applying Vulcan Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Maharaj Singh, State of Orissa v. Damodar Das, S. Rajan v. State of Kerala, Major (Retd.) Inder Singh Rekhi v. Delhi Development Authority, and Oriental Building and Furnishing Co. Ltd. v. Union of India, the Court held that the accrual date depends on the facts and that genuine negotiations to resolve a matter amicably do not, merely because differences have surfaced, mean that the right to apply has accrued. The Court also referred to Hughes v. Metropolitan Railway Co. on negotiations for settlement.

rule.if: arbitration_referral_application and amicable_negotiations_continued and no_unequivocal_claim_denial and application_filed_within_limitation_after_negotiations_end

predicates.arbitration_referral_application: A party applied for a court-supervised reference of an arbitration dispute.
predicates.amicable_negotiations_continued: The parties continued communicating and making genuine efforts to resolve the matter amicably.
predicates.no_unequivocal_claim_denial: The opposing party had not unequivocally denied or repudiated the claim while those efforts continued.
predicates.application_filed_within_limitation_afte: The application was filed within the applicable limitation period measured from the end of the parties’ negotiations.

issues.definition: When an arbitration-referral application follows continuing amicable negotiations without an unequivocal denial, it is not time-barred if it is filed within the applicable limitation period after those negotiations end.

issues.legal_issue: A dispute for arbitration requires an asserted claim and its denial or repudiation; delay, inaction, or unresolved efforts to work out an arrangement do not alone establish that a dispute has arisen.
material_facts: The parties’ representatives were appointed to work out a distribution, but the Court found that this did not itself establish a dispute requiring adjudication.
The correspondence concerning the distribution reflected continuing efforts to resolve matters amicably, and the Court found no earlier unequivocal denial of the claim to distribute the properties.
The Court treated the dispute as having arisen only after the parties’ attempts to settle the matter had failed.
issues.conclusion: The appointment of nominees and the failure to complete distribution did not, without a denial or repudiation of a claim, establish that a dispute had arisen; the dispute arose only when amicable resolution was no longer being pursued successfully.
issues.legal_principle: In Major (Retd.) Inder Singh Rekhi v. Delhi Development Authority, the Court held that a dispute requires a claim by one party and denial or repudiation by the other; mere failure or inaction does not suffice. State of Orissa v. Damodar Das likewise links accrual to an unequivocal denial of a claim. Whether a dispute has arisen is a question of fact to be determined in the circumstances of each case, as recognized in S. Rajan v. State of Kerala.

predicates.arbitration_dispute_proceeding: The matter concerns whether a dispute is available for reference to arbitration.
predicates.claim_asserted: One party communicated a claim to the other party.
predicates.claim_unequivocally_denied: The other party unequivocally rejected or repudiated that claim.

issues.definition: In an arbitration dispute proceeding, an arbitrable dispute has arisen when one party asserts a claim and the other unequivocally denies it.

issues.legal_issue: A bona fide family arrangement made to resolve or avoid family disputes should be favored and enforced rather than defeated on technical grounds.
material_facts: The partnership was dissolved through an arrangement among members of a family, including terms for distributing the family’s immovable properties.
The parties’ dispute concerned implementing that arrangement and distributing the properties.
The Court considered that enforcement of the arrangement would assist in resolving the family dispute and maintaining peace and harmony.
issues.conclusion: Technical considerations should give way to peace and harmony in enforcing a bona fide family arrangement or settlement.
issues.legal_principle: The Court relied on the special equity applicable to family arrangements and on Ram Charan Das v. Girjanadini Devi, Lala Khunni Lal v. Kunwar Gobind Krishna Nairain, Sahu Madho Das v. Pandit Mukand Ram, Maturi Pullaiah v. Maturi Narasimham, Krishna Biharilal v. Gulabchand, S. Shanmugam Pillai v. K. Shanmugam Pillai, Kale v. Deputy Director of Consolidation, and K.K. Modi v. K.N. Modi. Those authorities recognize that bona fide arrangements to resolve existing or possible family disputes, preserve harmony, or prevent future disputes should generally be upheld.

predicates.family_settlement_proceeding: The proceeding concerns an arrangement among members of a family to resolve or prevent disputes.
predicates.bona_fide_family_arrangement: The family members made the arrangement honestly to settle claims or preserve peace and harmony in the family.

issues.definition: In a family-settlement proceeding, courts favor enforcement when the family arrangement was made bona fide.

issues.legal_issue: Where a long-running family arbitration dispute remains unresolved and further remittal would cause additional delay, the Court may appoint a sole arbitrator directly to decide disputes within the arbitration agreement.
material_facts: The parties had an arbitration agreement covering disputes concerning the dissolution and distribution of the partnership’s assets.
The dispute had remained unresolved for many years, and attempts at conciliation had failed.
Some parties remained in possession and enjoyment of valuable properties while distribution was delayed.
The Court concluded that remitting the matter for further steps to appoint an arbitrator would risk further delay.
issues.conclusion: The Court appointed a sole arbitrator directly to resolve the disputes covered by the arbitration agreement.
issues.legal_principle: The arbitration clause provided for arbitration of disputes within its scope. In light of the prolonged dispute, failed conciliation, and risk of further delay, the Court appointed a sole arbitrator rather than remitting the matter for further appointment steps. The Court directed that the arbitration proceed under the Arbitration Act, 1940 or any statutory modification or re-enactment applicable under the agreement.

rule.if: arbitration_appeal and arbitration_clause_covers_dispute and prolonged_unresolved_dispute and conciliation_failed and remittal_would_risk_further_delay

predicates.arbitration_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning a dispute referred to arbitration.
predicates.arbitration_clause_covers_dispute: The parties agreed to arbitrate disputes of the kind before the Court.
predicates.prolonged_unresolved_dispute: The arbitration dispute had remained unresolved for an extended period.
predicates.conciliation_failed: The parties’ attempt to resolve the dispute through conciliation did not succeed.
predicates.remittal_would_risk_further_delay: Sending the matter back for further appointment steps would risk prolonging resolution.

issues.definition: In an arbitration appeal, the Court appoints a sole arbitrator directly when the clause covers the dispute, it has remained unresolved for an extended period, conciliation has failed, and remittal would risk further delay.
